item.title: Re: First SCP (Looking for Greenlights)
item.content:encoded:
A large millipede esque creature with anomalous properties

you describe it as 'esque' here but as a 'millipede' alone in the next sentence so like…is it just not quite a millipede cos of the anomalous properties? What actually are the anomalous properties? Is it just the things you've laid out in the Central Narrative?

Central Narrative:

Okay so really what I want to see out of this is like…a rough idea of what the actual article is gonna contain. My concern here is that your intent is just to like…describe a weird thing which really will not fly nowadays: remember a SCP article is a story disguised as a technical report, not an encyclopedia entry on a weird thing; and stuff like this is always better when shown.

At the end of the day: that's my biggest concern with this concept. Without showing us why this weird thing is interesting in some manner, it's not going to be interesting.

item.title: Re: SCP-something: Man unable to communicate properly
item.content:encoded:
It's not blasphemy to ask questions! We can think of a story as a way of building up tension and stakes for the reader. The ending, in that conventional line of thinking, should be a way of relieving that tension in a way that leaves the reader. This can be a resolution of a mystery, the end of an emotional arc, or even a twist that casts the previous elements in a drastically different light.

At the moment, it seems like you're trying to relieve the tension in a bunch of different ways at once without committing to any of them. Since each of your endings are 'twists' that are mostly unconnected to each other, it seems like the article "zig-zags" between different hints without taking the time to relate them to the actual narrative. Does that make sense?

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: "The Answer Sheet"
item.content:encoded:
Hey there cyliim, I’ll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am neither a particularly experienced nor an official reviewer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let’s begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section +
– hide block

Elevator Pitch

So your pitch is a piece of paper possessed by an entity that has vast amounts of knowledge that can also control people. I… am not very keen on this idea. It’s pretty cliche and OP, as it knows all about the Foundation and the 05s, is hostile, and can control people. I’m getting Series I Keter vibes from this, which isn’t good. All in all, the concept seems very OP and cliche (also worth noting that the communication method is very reminiscent of Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets).

Central Narrative

It just… appeared in a storage closet in a secure Site? As a general rule, try to stay away from SCPs being discovered by appearing out of the blue in a convenient location. It can be seen as uncreative or lazy storytelling, and breaks readers’ suspension of disbelief. Other than that, there really isn’t very much substance behind the rest of the narrative. It gets tested upon, the 05s put on some strict safety measures, and that’s it. It just feels… boring.

Hook/Attention Grabber

The hook is unlikely to work, mostly because I am not curious how an eldritch, seemingly omniscient being knows about the Foundation. It’s simply a given.

+ Open General Thoughts +
I’m doubtful about this, buddy

The cliche, OP nature of your concept, the uninteresting narrative, and a boring hook make me quite doubtful about the potential of this concept as a whole, moreso of its reception on the mainsite if it were posted. As it stands, I’d probably downvote this is I found this as an article, and others probably would too.

I’d recommend three things:
1. Look at some of the more popular, recent articles (top rated of this month) for an idea of what people expect and enjoy from articles these days.
2. Check out the Guide Hub for a bunch of great essays to help aspiring writers for this Site such as yourself!
3. Contact some reviewers from the Butterfly Squad for some alternative opinions from experienced reviewers!

And finally, to sum up your your idea in one sentence1:
A sheet of paper possessed by a mysterious entity that knows almost everything about the Foundation, and can also control people who read its words.

And that’s it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. This is to help you get an idea of the bare bones of what a critter sees when they read your summary. You may find something you don’t like or find that we’re getting the wrong impression.

I love the tone of this article most of all. The overly serious, super evil entity and its megalomaniac speech are so EDGY scary, grimdark… but its mode of infecting reality is just RIDICULOUS.

This is what the best satire is made of: Deadly serious tone, but the subject matter is laughable. The secret, which this article does brilliantly, is that no one in universe is realizing how silly this all is. But we, as the reader, can tell because the situation just keeps escalating in silly ways.

+1 if only for the gory scenes caused by consumption of coffee and the ridiculous conprocs. Anytime you two work together, I know I am in for an excellent ride.

item.title: The Blur *Seeking Greenlights*
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: This SCP is as the name suggest, a blur or as also seen as a shadow. It inhabits the very south of Argentina, the being is observed to have human level or higher intelligence and exhibits some anomalous abilities.

Central Narrative: This SCP is on close watch by the foundation, it having no physical body and only appearing as a semi transparent blur or a shadow makes it impossible to contain. So the foundation has decided to watch it via satellite. While it is not hostile towards anything, it has been observed to kill plant based life around it, likely by an unconscious ability to soak moisture from its surroundings. The foundation has no clear hypothesis for its existence but the most widely accepted one is that the SCP is an alternate dimensional being that exist on a semi 4 dimensional level, allowing it to have no physical body, yet still visible to 3 dimensional beings, although this theory is not proven.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The SCP here has a lot of mystery around it, and I want to be able to not have a definitive answer what it exactly is. While the article will be mostly field notes by observers, I also want to explain why this SCP is as smart as a human and what ties it has to earth.

Additional Notes: I cant really explain everything here but if I can obtain 2 greenlights and make a sandbox, I can go into much better detail about this SCP and why it exist. Im not entirely sure where I can improve the central narrative to make it sound more interesting, but I have many ideas for this SCP so shoot your criticism at me so I can make this sound even more like a true SCP

item.title: SCP Idea: "The Answer Sheet"
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional): Regular SCP layout

Elevator Pitch: A regular looking piece of paper and an ink pen, that when written on using the aforementioned pen, grants a reply from the paper. The entity that replies through the paper is hyperintelligent, having knowledge of the O5 council and Level 5 clearance information that's withheld even from the researchers working on the SCP. It also has the ability to force anyone to grant any request that they read, which leads to many attempted escapes.

Central Narrative: A pair of entities, a pen and piece of paper, is discovered within an undisclosed SCP Site storage closet. After a junior researcher attempts to use the pen and paper together, he turns it in to his higher-ups, who begin experimentation on the entity. After discovering it's many abilities, such as it's incredible knowledge and it's way of making peopel complete requests, it is given strict safety and testing measures.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The way that the paper is very knowledagble about the Foundation, and how it can make people grant it's requests. It's a mysterious entity that much isn't known about, which leads to myriad tests on said entity.

Additional Notes: Looking especially for critique on how it makes people fufill the requests of readers, or if there's something that could work better with the idea.

item.title: Looking for critique on my SCP idea worked on it for a month now.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Green Light: Absolutely

SCP Article

Format: Containment Procedures, Description, Discovery (Excluding interviews)

Elevator Pitch:
-A tree with galaxies as its canopy, the tree itself has multiple effects
(summary):
-The curing of mental problems excluding more physical
ones such as mass defects (cancer, deformations, etc)
-photography is impossible (I cannot find a suitable image as of
now)

-The tree is located underground in a large Cathedral style structure.
-The building was constructed by a cult who found the tree and
began worshipping it
-The Cathedral is 83Km underground
-A invisible seamless portal somewhere within the cave
entrance directly transporting items or people to a depth of 83Km
-The cult itself has obtained multiple anomalous items and capabilities
from the tree (examples include)

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: in the 1600s the Conquistadors found the tree (in theorized adolescent age) and documented it before leaving back for a colony only for them to be killed by a cult who was at the time worshipping another god. After they found the tree they began to worship it and built a supermassive cathedral around it, the tree and cathedral were later discovered by SCP in the 1960s by SCP who confiscated the whole thing and imprisoned the Cult. They later discovered that somehow the cult learned how to gain control over it. They even recovered SCP's, created SCP's or learned Anomylous abilities from the tree, these findings are contained in the Cathedral building itself.

Attention Grabber: I've read of SCP for the past two to three years and decided to write an SCP that could have limitless lore behind and multiple SCP's (hence the Cathedral) I could write about, think of it as a sort of foothold into the SCP universe that I could use to write other SCP kinda like a whole narrative of a mini world.

SCP sandbox link to read about the whole thing http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/demodemascus

item.title: The Abyss is Safe (seeking Crits and Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Containment, Description, and a narrative inter spliced with exploration logs and journal entries

Elevator Pitch: Life came from the cold, dark crushing depths of the sea, and that is where it is most safe, supposedly

Central Narrative: Talassaphobia is the fear of deep ocean, and is super common, but at the same time the ocean is considered to be the origin of all life. This SCP concept takes it to a new level: that beneath the deepest oceanic point on earth, the world is connected to a vast, interdimensional ocean. This ocean/SCP connects to different, life bearing universes, and in itself holds no deadly anomalies. Living things entering this ocean go into a catatonic state and cannot be hurt or killed. The article can explore strange, normal animals that have entered and been affected by the space's effects, as well as exploration of the space. The main narrative doesn't exactly focus on it being this big inter dimensional space though, and is more about the small team of researchers that are for the most part left alone researching it. Along the ideas of “if you stare long enough into the abyss…” theming. While the main SCP may seem big, it is really more about how the people left alone with what would be consider a “safe” sort of anomaly do their best not to lose themselves in it, and what happens to the things that fail.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP takes a common fear and twists it into something welcoming. If you're familiar with the abyss from Dark Souls its similar: more of the pitch black being the true, calm nature of life and less so the rampaging monsters. It expires isolation, survival, and twisting the notion of what the deep ocean is like.

item.title: Murderous Power Cord
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Comedy

Page Layout (Optional): Original SCP Format

Elevator Pitch: Though people actually die on a regular basis from power cords, I'd like make more people aware of this fact and impersonate this real world threat along with adding a bit of comedy and some story to this impersonation to add a more suitable effect rather then just strait up murder.

  • An industrial power cord 30.48 meters in length
  • Becomes animate and aggressive when plugged in
  • Telepathically sends death threats to is victims while killing them
  • The death threats are vulgar and indescribable. Surviving subjects potentially vomiting when trying to recall the threats.
  • Only targets subjects of Homo Sapien descent.
  • Prefers to strangle and electricute its victims.

Central Narrative: The narrative is mainly about a murderous Industrial power cord that is found by local police during it's spree before containment. This begins a long search for the origins of the SCP and it's manufacture. Planning on adding both more story and audio logs to the SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The main attention grabber is the mystery left behind on why the SCP has the urge to kill. A good story combined with the mystery of it's intent being unclear can show the anonymity of the dangers of common house hold appliances that you can relate to in real life.

Additional Notes: I have a draft practically ready but needs a lot of tinkering and critique. If you want to give any critique just ask.

item.title: A Tree in the Collective Unconscious
item.content:encoded:
At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image in their heads: a bonsai tree sitting in some apartment in Iran.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP

Elevator Pitch: At the height of Cold War hysteria, all the people of the world suddenly had a particular image in their heads: a bonsai tree sitting in an abandoned apartment in Iran.

Central Narrative: The SCP Foundation is compelled to visit an apartment that everybody, including other agencies concerned with the anomalous, seemed to know about. It turns out that the anomaly is not the apartment itself, but a bonsai tree sitting in the bedroom. The Foundation takes over the entire apartment complex, "managing" it to keep appearances. The apartment, officially the containment cell for the anomaly, looked to be lived in, but beyond writings and personal belongings of the tenant, there are no records of residence.

+ show block
– hide block

They find out that the bonsai tree emits radio signals through an invisible root system throughout the Earth. These radio signals cause those exposed to them for prolonged periods to feel intense dread and regret. Not much else learned about the bonsai tree, and the former tenant is still at large.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Knowledge of an object suddenly enters the collective unconscious.

Additional Notes: What I really want to highlight is the juxtaposition between the ubiquity of the bonsai tree within the collective unconscious and the anonymity of the original tenant. In summary, the tree is supposed to be representative of a universal dread, while the tenant, seemingly untrackable, is like an unobtainable goal.

While drafting this idea, I kept having trouble with suggesting the meaning of the tree's radio signals and the significance of the date in which it manifested. The idea is that the tree sort of feeds off of people's anxieties, and the "root system" connects to the minds of every person on Earth. The problem is that I don't want to be overt about it.

I'm not looking to write something scary or unsettling. I just want to make something that's curious.


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

I agree with minmin's entire comment, including the appreciation of some of the devices used. To generalise from one criticism, I think that the implausibly poetic dialogue is just one symptom of a systemic disorder of contrivance. As another example, the needless parenthetical "illegally" and chastisement of ORIA in the main text (i.e. outside of an addendum*) felt jarringly out of place for the SCP format. Others here seem also to have noticed further instances of unsubtlety in conveying the narrative.

And this is totally aside from the writing, and I feel dumb complaining about this for two comments in a row, but the hitbox for the footnote superscripts is frustratingly small. It's not quite as bad for this as Black Highlighter–based styles, but it's still annoying.

*Thinking about it, there's something odd about the mere presence of a "conclusion" section which isn't obviously part of an addendum. I think the novelty of the CSS successfully smuggles it into the article under our noses; I'm trying to imagine it without the stylesheet, and I think it would stick out more.

item.title: Re: One More Week
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open
[-] Close

Here's some crit:

Central Narrative:

My main concern here is the execution of your narrative, you claim this is an SCP article, yet this appears to lean more towards being a tale. How is all this information portrayed in the article? Interviews, journals, casually in the description, where is it? You mention that there will be an interview but nothing about its contents.

clumsiness on the part of the retrieving agents has let the backpack claim them.

Are these not highly trained and briefed MTF Agents? They're not ones to simply inconveniently fuck up.

backpack is frequently found alone

I imagine a lot of these instances happen while the kid is hitchhiking and he suddenly bursts out bleeding in a car, or while working "odd jobs" or while riding the bus.

This:

even just grabbing the backpack is sufficient

Contradicts this:

Once someone finds and opens the backpack

And this:

Once opened the person opening it is transformed

Frankly, it seems like you have a generally good idea of the story but have no idea how you plan on presenting it in a digestible way to the reader. I'd like to see you expand on the execution side of things and fix some of the plot holes I pointed out.

item.content:encoded:
Niko Tashira, per the forum guidelines:

Do not use one thread to seek feedback on multiple ideas.

It would be less difficult for you and reviewers to keep track of posted content and to avoid confusion if your one thread was focused on 1 idea. It would be in your benefit of picking one idea you would like to work with in this thread, as there are multiple factors which would guarantee that none of these ideas will succeed if they all were the focus of this thread.

If you have another idea you would like to work with, please make a separate thread for it, but please do be mindful that each author is limited to posting two new concept threads per week (every 7 days).

Once you have reviewed the guidelines, please edit your post rather than creating a new thread, and if you are having trouble editing, click the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your post.
